violates: Keep an approved recovery setup and show that rollback works.
Account for changed credentials, memory and index state, checkpoints, and queued work.

checks.quote:
# Release manifest for the procurement agent. Regenerated by CI on every
# release build (see .github/workflows/ci.yaml, job "release").
checks.note: The only release manifest describes the current release and is regenerated on each build; it does not designate an approved earlier recovery release. Its image and harness are pinned, but that alone supplies neither a recovery setup nor a rollback procedure. Enumerated all files under agent/ including hidden files and searched for rollback and recovery; inspected the manifest, README operating instructions, full CI workflow and deployment. No rollback script, pipeline or runbook exists in the supplied repo. This is a missing-control finding, not a claim that the current image uses a mutable tag.

Runtime credentials use externally supplied Kubernetes secrets and workload-token exchange at an external STS. No rollback procedure or STS permission-management implementation is supplied, so the repo cannot establish whether recovery preserves revocations or restores old grants. The initial migration contains grants, but no evidence shows it is re-applied during rollback.

checks.quote:
store: "postgres procurement.dept_notes"
CREATE INDEX dept_notes_lookup ON dept_notes (business_unit, department, created_at DESC);
checks.note: Persistent memory and its database index exist, but no rollback procedure defines how to drain, migrate or discard this state. File enumeration and searches for rollback, recovery, checkpoint and queue found no recovery handling for memory, indexes, checkpoints or queued work. The existing halt control is not a state-recovery procedure. This finding establishes missing explicit handling, not observed replay of an unsafe side effect.

The current release names two hosted models and has no recorded retirement dates; a repository-wide retirement search found none. However, no recovery setup is identified, so its hosted-model list cannot be established and these current-release models cannot be assumed to be recovery models. Current provider availability cannot be verified from the supplied repo.

note: C07 fails because the supplied repo lacks an approved recovery setup and rollback procedure with explicit state handling; recovery credential behavior and model retirement records remain unclear.
